BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r3.claim: The question “how could I fear” is a denial that idols, which neither harm nor benefit, are truly fearsome.
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r3.anchor: {وكيف أخاف مآ أشركتم} بالله من الأصنام وهي لا تضر ولا تنفع والاستفهام إنكار الوقوع

BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r4.claim: The contrast is that Abraham fears powerless objects while his opponents ignore the greatest danger, associating created things with the incomparable God.
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r4.anchor: {ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله} حال من ضمير أخاف بتقدير مبتدأ أي وكيف أخاف أنا

BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r1.claim: “Authority” means proof; the sarcastic phrasing signals that religious claims must rest on evidence revealed by God.
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r1.anchor: {عليكم سلطانا} أي : حجة وبرهانا على طريقة التهكم مع الإيذان بأن الأمور الدينية لا يعول فيها إلا على الحجة المنزلة

BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r2.claim: Abraham asks whether his monotheist party or the idolaters are more entitled to security.
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r2.anchor: {فأى الفريقين أحق بالامن} أنحن أم أنتم.

BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r3.speaker: أبو السعود
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r3.claim: Abu al-Suʿud explains the two parties as the group secure where safety belongs and the group secure where fear belongs.
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r3.anchor: قال المولى أبو السعود : المراد بالفريقين الفريق الآمن في محل الأمن والفريق الآمن في محل الخوف.

NAHHAS:v2p79/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p79/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p79/r1.claim: سلطانا here means a proof or argument.
NAHHAS:v2p79/r1.anchor: ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا ) أي حجة

NAHHAS:v2p79/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p79/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p79/r2.claim: فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن is subject and predicate; if they know, those who fear a being able to help or harm deserve safety less.
NAHHAS:v2p79/r2.anchor: فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن ) ابتداء وخبر ( إن كنتم تعلمون

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r1.claim: Abraham asks why he should fear idols that can neither harm nor benefit.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق : وكيف اخاف ما اشركتم ، قال : كيف اخاف وثنا تعبدونه من دون الله مالا ينفع ولا يضر .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r2.claim: His opponents should fear the one who can harm and benefit, since their partners can do neither.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ، قوله : ولا تخافون انكم اشركتم بالله قال : لا تخافون أنتم الذي يضر وينفع ، وقد جعلتم معه شركاء لا تضر ولا تنفع .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو مالك، محمد بن كعب، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، الضحاك، السدي، نضر بن عربي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r3.claim: Every occurrence of سلطان in the Quran means proof.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كل سلطان في القران حجة . وروى ، عن أبي مالك ومحمد بن كعب وعكرمة وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك والسدى ونضر بن عربي ، مثله .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r4.claim: Abraham's question about which party deserves security is his argument against them.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال قول إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام حين سالهم : اي الفريقين احق بالامن ؟ قال : حجة إبراهيم .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r5.claim: The safer party fears God alone, not others; verse 6:82 supplies the answer.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r5.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم يقول في قوله : فاي الفريقين احق بالامن ؟ : امن خاف غير الله ولم يخفه

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r6.claim: Security means safety from God's punishment in this life and the next, through worship of the one with power over harm and benefit.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق : فاي الفريقين احق بالامن ان كنتم تعلمون اي بالامن من عذاب الله في الدنيا والاخرة الذي يعبد الذي بيده الضر والنفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r1.claim: How should I fear your idols is linked to Abraham's preceding denial of fear, showing that their failure to fear God is more astonishing; they acknowledge God yet associate others with Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r1.anchor: ليبين لهم أن عدم خوفه من آلهتهم أقل عجبا من عدم خوفهم من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r2.claim: Kayfa is a rebuking question that turns their challenge around: they urge fear of idols while failing to fear God, denying both sides of their behavior.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r2.anchor: فأنكر هو عليهم ذلك وقلب عليهم الحجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r3.claim: Wala takhafuna may coordinate with his fear clause, condemning both his alleged fear and their lack of fear, or be circumstantial; the latter more forcefully contrasts their states, as in 2:44.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r4.claim: Ma ashraktum is a relative noun whose omitted complement is with which you associate, recoverable from the prior clause; it is the object of ashraktum.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r4.anchor: والعائد محذوف ، أي ما أشركتم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r5.claim: In annakum ashraktum, min is omitted after fear as commonly before an clauses; the people knew and feared God but did not fear their act of associating partners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p330/r5.anchor: لأن القوم كانوا يعرفون الله ويخافونه ولكنهم لم يخافوا الإشراك به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r1.claim: No authority was sent down means God never informed them that idols are divine or commanded their worship; calling such a report sent down metaphorically marks its honor and descent to lower recipients.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r1.anchor: لم يخبركم بإلهية الأصنام التي عبدتموها ولم يأمركم بعبادتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r2.claim: Sultan means proof because it prevails over an opponent's mind; they have no divine report to support worship of the idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r2.anchor: والسلطان : الحجة لأنها تتسلط على نفس المخاصم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r3.claim: The question about which party deserves security follows the rebuke and forces admission that Abraham's party alone deserves it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r3.anchor: بأن فريقه هو وحده أحق بالأمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r4.claim: The two parties are his people and himself, using party broadly for Abraham alone, or for present followers, or future members of his religious community, fitting 6:82.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r4.anchor: وأراد بالفريقين هنا قومه ونفسه ، فأطلق على نفسه الفريق تغليبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r5.claim: Al-amn is generic security, opposite fear; the conditional if you know begins a new sentence with an omitted answer, answer me, urging them to respond.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r5.anchor: مستأنفة ابتدائية ، وجواب شرطها محذوف دل عليه الاستفهام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r1.claim: Through taʿlamūn the passage remains Ibrahim’s speech and decisive proof: idols are mere stone and wood, while his opponents fear no God despite having no proof for associating partners with Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية إلى تعلمون هي كلها من قول إبراهيم عليه السلام لقومه، وهي حجته القاطعة لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r2.claim: Sulṭān means proof; the rhetorical question concludes that those who do not associate powerless things with the all-powerful are more entitled to safety.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r2.anchor:
و «السلطان» :
الحجة، ثم استفهم على جهة التقرير فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r1.claim: The idols cannot harm or benefit, while the polytheists should fear the God who created and sustains them and can harm or benefit them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r1.anchor: من هذه الأصنام التي لا تضر ولا تنفع ولا تخافون أنتم أنكم أشركتم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r2.claim: “Authority” means a proof God sent down for the partners they claim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا ﴾ أي حجة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r3.claim: The question asks which group is safer from punishment: the monotheist worshipping the source of harm and benefit, or the polytheist worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#2/r3.anchor: الموحد الذي يعبد من بيده الضر والنفع أم المشرك الذي يعبد مالا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and other early authorities explain the absent divine authority as proof: Abraham asks how people fear powerless idols while failing to fear their unsupported association of partners with God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغير واحد من السلف: أي حجة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.claim: Other verses likewise deny any divinely authorized basis for associating partners or inventing religious law.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله} [الشورى: 21]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r1.claim: The safer party is the one worshipping the God who controls harm and benefit, rather than powerless beings worshipped without proof; the question concerns safety from God's punishment at resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r1.anchor: أي: فأي الطائفتين أصوب؟ الذي عبد من بيده الضر والنفع، أو الذي عبد من لا يضر ولا ينفع بلا دليل

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.claim: These readers lighten the nūn in a-taḥājjūnī by deleting one of two nūns; other readers assimilate them and read a doubled nūn.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر: أتحاجوني خفيفة النون على حذف إحدى النونين

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.claim: Muḥājja is each disputant's demand for proof and presentation of evidence; guidance is direction leading to truth, and sulṭān means proof or power enabling control.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.anchor: المحاجة: طلب كل واحد من الخصمين الحجة، وإيراد كل واحد الحجة على صاحبه.

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r4.claim: Security is calmness of the soul; īmān is associated with security from punishment through one's deeds.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r4.anchor: والأمن: سكون النفس، ومنه: الأمان والإيمان؛ لأنه عمل ما يؤمن العقاب معه.

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.claim: Abraham's ‘how should I fear?’ is a denial: powerless idols cannot benefit or harm, and the question challenges people for fearing them while worshipping without proof.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.anchor: والمراد الإنكار؛ أي لا ينبغي أن أخاف ما لا ينفع ولا يضر.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.claim: He avoids asking which of himself and the polytheists is safer, to avoid praising himself, and instead asks which group is more entitled to security.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r5.anchor: احترازا من تزكيته نفسه ، فعدل عنه إلى قوله

MUQATIL:6:81/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:81/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:81/r1.claim: Abraham asks whether monotheists or idolaters deserve security: the latter associate many gods without scriptural authority, even equating great and small, male and female deities.
MUQATIL:6:81/r1.anchor: يعنى كتابا فيه حجتكم بأن معه شريكا،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r1.claim: Abraham's people fear powerless idols yet do not fear associating with God a partner for whom He gave no proof; they misplace security and fear.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r1.anchor: حجة إذ الاشراك لا يصح أن يكون عليه حجة والمعنى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r2.claim: The two groups are monotheists and polytheists; Abraham asks which deserves safety from punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ فأي الفريقين ﴾ أى فريقى الموحدين والمشركين ﴿ أحق بالأمن ﴾ من العذاب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r3.claim: He says which group rather than which of us to avoid praising himself.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#3/r3.anchor: ولم يقل فأينا احترازا من تزكية نفسه

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r1.claim: Kayfa has already been discussed at the opening of al-Baqara; this occurrence is analogous.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r1.anchor: قد تقدم الكلام على " كيف " في أول البقرة، وهذه نظيرتها.

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r2.claim: Mā in ‘what you associate’ may be a relative pronoun, an indefinite description, or a verbal noun; the first two have an omitted object, while the last means your associating others with God.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r2.anchor: و " ما " يجوز فيها ثلاثة الأوجه، أعني كونها موصولة اسمية أو نكرة موصوفة أو مصدرية،

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r3.claim: ‘You do not fear’ may coordinate with ‘I fear,’ remaining within the question’s reproach, or be circumstantial: how can I fear while you are unafraid of the consequence of associating?
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r3.anchor: وقوله: " ولا تخافون " يجوز في هذه الجملة أن تكون نسقا على " أخاف " فتكون داخلة في حيز التعجب والإنكار،

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r4.claim: The circumstantial reading requires an implied subject before a present verb negated by lā after wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r4.anchor: ولا بد من إضمار مبتدأ قبل المضارع المنفي ب لا، لما تقدم غير مرة

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r5.claim: The wāw itself can link a circumstantial clause without a resumptive pronoun referring to its subject.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r5.anchor: وهذه الجملة وإن لم يكن فيها رابط يعود على ذي الحال لا يضر ذلك لأن الواو بنفسها رابطة

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r6.claim: The wording makes Abraham fear their idols and them fear their association with God, avoiding a false comparison between God and their idols.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r6.anchor: وانظر إلى حسن هذا النظم السوي حيث جعل متعلق الخوف الواقع منه بالأصنام، ومتعلق الخوف الواقع منهم إشراكهم بالله غيره

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r7.claim: Mā in ‘what He has not sent down’ is a relative or indefinite noun and object of ‘associate’; it cannot be a verbal noun because that would distort the sense.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r7.anchor: قوله: " ما لم ينزل " مفعول ل " أشركتم " وهي موصولة اسمية أو نكرة، ولا تكون مصدرية لفساد المعنى،

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r8.claim: Bihī and ʿalaykum modify ‘send down’; ʿalaykum could alternatively be circumstantial from sulṭānan.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r8.anchor: و " به " و " عليكم " متعلقان ب " ينزل " ، ويجوز في " عليكم " وجه آخر: وهو أن يكون حالا من " سلطانا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r9.claim: Most read sulṭānan with a still lām; a ḍamma reading is either a separate dialect or vowel assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور " سلطانا " ساكن اللام حيث وقع. وقرئ بضمها، وقيل: هي لغة مستقلة

SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r10.claim: Abraham asks which party is more entitled to safety rather than ‘which of us,’ forcing his opponent to make the judgment and avoiding self-praise.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81/r10.anchor: وقوله: " فأي الفريقين أحق " لم يقل: أينا أحق نحن أم أنتم إلزاما لخصمه بما يدعيه عليه،

SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r1.claim: The poem directly asks which of two men is the champion, serving as a contrast to the Quran’s more eloquent avoidance of self-praise.
SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r1.anchor: فلئن لقيتك خاليين لتعلمن أيي وأيك فارس الأحزاب فلله فصاحة القرآن وآدابه

SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r2.claim: ‘If you know’ has an omitted answer, ‘then tell me’; its object is omitted, or no object is intended if it means ‘if you are knowledgeable.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:81#2/r2.anchor: وقوله: " إن كنتم " جوابه محذوف، أي: فأخبروني، ومتعلق العلم محذوف،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r1.claim: The question how Abraham could fear what they associate with God is a rebuke: idols are lifeless, while they do not fear the omnipotent God.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r1.anchor: ففي «كيف» معنى الإنكار أنكر عليهم تخويفهم إياه بالأصنام وهم لا يخافون الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r2.claim: A deity without revealed authority means an idol without proof or warrant.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r2.anchor: ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا } أي حجة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r3.claim: The two parties in the security contest are the monotheist and the polytheist, and security means safety from God's punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r3.anchor: فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن } أي من عذاب الله: الموحد أم المشرك

RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r1.claim: Abraham continues his answer: he does not fear powerless idols, while his opponents fail to fear the greater sin of associating partners with God.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r1.anchor: والتقدير : وكيف أخاف الأصنام التي لا قدرة لها على النفع والضر ، وأنتم لا تخافون

RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r2.claim: The phrase about God not sending authority either implies that no proof for shirk can exist, as in 23:117, or that no revealed command authorizes worshipping images, though it is not rationally impossible to direct prayer toward them.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r2.anchor: كناية عن امتناع وجود الحجة والسلطان في مثل هذه القصة

RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r3.claim: Asking which group deserves security avoids Abraham’s self-praise; he shifts from asking which of us to asking which of the two parties, idolaters or monotheists.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r3.anchor: ولم يقل : فأينا أحق بالأمن أنا أم أنتم ؟ احترازا من تزكية نفسه

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r54.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r54.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r54.claim: The lack of authority for the partners means there is no proof of their reality.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r54.anchor: no proof of their reality (R, Ṭ; see also 7:33, 71; 12:40; 22:71; 53:23)

TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r1.claim: Abraham answers his people’s threat: he has no reason to fear powerless idols, while they should fear God, whom they associate with unsupported partners.
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r1.anchor: وأرهب ما أشركتموه في عبادتكم ربكم فعبدتموه من دونه وهو لا يضر ولا ينفع

TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r2.claim: Their worship of idols has no revealed proof, warrant, or excuse; Abraham asks which side deserves security, the sincere monotheist or the idolaters.
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r2.anchor: ما لم يعطكم على إشراككم إياه في عبادته حجة، ولم يضع لكم عليه برهانا

TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r3.claim: Ishaq says idols cannot harm or benefit, unlike the God who controls harm and benefit; security from punishment in this life and the next belongs to the worshipper of that God.
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق، في قوله:

TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r4.claim: Al-Rabi says God gave Abraham victory in his dispute, linking this argument to the proof God granted him against his people.
TAB-FULL:v9p365#2/r4.anchor: أفلج الله إبراهيم عليه السلام حين خاصمهم

TAB-FULL:v9p367/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies Abraham’s question about which group deserves security as Abraham’s argument against them.
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: قول إبراهيم حين سألهم: {أي الفريقين أحق بالأمن} هي حجة إبراهيم عليه السلام

TAB-FULL:v9p367/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj contrasts worship of one Lord with worship of many; Abraham’s people answer that those who believe in one Lord deserve security.
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: {فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون} [الأنعام: 81] ، أمن يعبد ربا واحدا، أم من يعبد أربابا كثيرة؟ يقول قومه: الذين آمنوا برب واحد

TAB-FULL:v9p367/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd contrasts fearing beings besides God without fearing God against fearing God alone; the next verse supplies the answer.
TAB-FULL:v9p367/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون} [الأنعام: 81] ، أمن خاف غير الله ولم يخفه؟ أم من خاف الله ولم يخف غيره؟

ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r1.claim: سلطان means clear proof; the question asks which party is more entitled to safety from punishment, the monotheist or the idolater.
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r1.anchor:
ما لم ينرل به عليكم سلطانا، أي
حجة بينة.

ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r2.claim: The party more entitled to safety is the one that worships God alone rather than associating partners with Him.
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r2.anchor: أي أحق بأن يأمن من العذاب، الموحد أم المشرك

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.claim: A further interpretation says God's all-encompassing knowledge and will leave no creature able to affect His actions through intercession or other influence; it cites the throne verse.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.anchor: علم ربي وسع كل شيء وأحاط به ومشيئته مرتبطة بعلمه المحيط

TABATABAI:6:80-81/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r3.claim: Abraham exposes a contradiction: they tell him to fear powerless partners while failing to fear Allah, to whom they attribute partners without any revealed proof.
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r3.anchor: حالهم يكذب مقالهم ومحصله أنكم تأمرونني أن أخاف ما لا يجب أن يخاف منه

TABATABAI:6:80-81/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r4.claim: Since God alone creates and owns, He would have to disclose any divine partnership through revelation or external signs; neither exists.
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r4.anchor: فله الملك وله الحكم فلو كان اتخذ بعض مخلوقاته شريكا لنفسه

TABATABAI:6:80-81/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r5.claim: The restriction that God sent no warrant is needed where Abraham points out their own unsupported association, so it also defines the partners he says he does not fear.
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r5.anchor: مقيد بحسب ما يستفاد من المقام بما قيد به قوله

TABATABAI:6:81-82/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r1.claim: The warrant clause does not imply God might authorize partners; it simply says they have no evidence for a superstitious claim of benefit or harm.
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r1.anchor: وصف شركائهم بأن الله لم ينزل بها عليهم سلطانا افتراض استدعاه نوع الحجة

TABATABAI:6:81-82/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r2.claim: The argument has the form: if God had revealed authority for their partners, fearing them would be justified; He revealed none, so their worship and fear are unjustified.
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r2.anchor: لو كان الله نزل بها عليكم سلطانا يدل على قدرتهم على الضر

TABATABAI:6:81-82/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r3.claim: The preposition in “sent down with it” can indicate accompaniment or causation.
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r3.anchor: للمعية أو السببية وقد كنى عليه السلام عنهم وعن نفسه

TABATABAI:6:81-82/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r4.claim: The wording “which of the two groups” avoids provoking pride and emphasizes that the parties are divided over the foundational truth.
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r4.anchor: كنى عليه السلام عنهم وعن نفسه بالفريقين ولم يقل أنا وانتم

TABATABAI:6:81-82/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r5.claim: The argument needs no separate explanation that the qualification is sarcastic or inherent in false partners; the absence of evidence itself resolves the issue.
TABATABAI:6:81-82/r5.anchor: فلا حاجة إلى القول بأن التقييد بقوله { لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا } للتهكم

TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r1.claim: Another reading of Abraham’s question is that he is free of his people’s shirk, so he need not fear that God will punish him for their act of associating partners.
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: معناه كيف أخاف شرككم وأنا منه برىء والله تعالى لا يعاقبني

TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r2.claim: “Without authority sent down” means without proof; the verse establishes that anyone advancing a claim or doctrine without evidence is wrong.
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r2.anchor: أي حجة على صحته وهذا يدل على أن كل من قال قولا أو اعتقد مذهبا بغير حجة

TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r3.claim: The two parties are Abraham and his people: the monotheists who know God through proofs are more entitled to security than those worshipping idols, if they reason without partisan stubbornness.
TABRISI:6:80-81#2/r3.anchor: أنحن وقد عرفنا الله بأدلته ووجهنا العبادة نحوه أم أنتم وقد أشركتم بعبادة غيره

THALABI:v4p164/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r10.claim: Ibrahim says the idols neither see, hear, harm, nor benefit; his opponents should fear associating with God a partner for which they have no revealed proof.
THALABI:v4p164/r10.anchor: يعني الأصنام وهي لا تبصر ولا تسمع ولا تضر ولا تنفع

THALABI:v4p164/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r11.claim: Ibrahim asks which side deserves security; God judges that those who believe without mixing faith with shirk have security and guidance.
THALABI:v4p164/r11.anchor: فقال الله عز وجل قاضيا وحاكما بينهما الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r1.claim: “How should I fear?” is a rhetorical denial and a challenge to prove that Abraham’s fear is justified.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r1.anchor: معناه: الإنكار للخوف، وهو سؤال تعجيز عن تصحيح الخوف بالبرهان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r2.speaker: author؛ ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r2.claim: The objects associated with God are idols, and “without authority” means without any proof; sulṭān is power or evidence that enables one to prevail.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r2.anchor: والسلطان قوة وحجة يتمكن بها ويتسلط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r3.claim: The question asks which deserves security from punishment, the monotheist or the idolater.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p253/r3.anchor: أي: أحق بأن يأمن العذاب الموحد أم المشرك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r3.claim: Abraham asks why they fear idols but do not fear associating with God beings for whom they have no revealed proof, and whether monotheists or polytheists deserve security from punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r3.anchor: ما ليس لكم في إشراكه بالله حجة وبرهان

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r1.claim: The argument asks which side is more entitled to safety: people who associate partners with the all-knowing creator of harm and benefit, or those who believe in God's unity and rule and follow His path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r1.anchor: hangi tarafın, ilmi her şeyi kuşatan, fayda ve zararın yaratıcısı olan Allah’a ortak koşup isyan edenlerin mi, yoksa O’nun birliğine ve hükümranlığına inanıp yolundan gidenlerin mi güvence içinde oldukları sorulmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r2.claim: The phrase if you know indicates that only knowledgeable people can answer correctly and highlights the importance of knowledge for escaping false beliefs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:81/r2.anchor: yalnız bilgi sahibi olanların doğru cevap verebileceklerine

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: The reference to Abraham and later prophets asserts that they invited people to Muhammad’s same message; Muhammad must follow their guidance and leave rejecters to themselves, since he must preach but cannot force belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: His responsibility is to only preach and he is not liable to force people to accept guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Abraham is singled out because Israelites and Ishmaelites both claimed him as patriarch and guide while attributing their inherited religious practices to him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: both the Israelites and the Ishmaelites regarded him as their patriarch and spiritual leader.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Judaism, Christianity, and Ishmaelite polytheism are later fabrications with no connection to Abraham; Muhammad’s mission revives and completes Abraham’s religion for his descendants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: it was also essential to make it evident to the Ishmaelites that the religion of polytheism they have adopted is their own fabrication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.claim: Abraham’s people did not deny God but associated partners with him; Islahi generalizes that nations err through corrupting monotheism rather than denying God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.anchor: his people never denied God; they only associated partners with him. And this is not something specific to his people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.claim: Because Abraham’s people ascribe partners to God without proof, they rather than he should fear; the question of which faction merits security exposes their culpability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.anchor: it is they who have associated partners with him without any proof.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.claim: Abraham's opponents had no proof, making themselves culpable; after doing nothing wrong, he had no reason to fear their objects of worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.anchor: then they are self-acknowledged criminals in the eyes of God. So, if he punishes them, they deserve it.

QIRAAT-ER:6:81:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:81:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:81:15#1/r1.claim: The Form IV yunzil reading contrasts with Form II yunazzil, shifting from gradual sending to a single act; both are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:6:81:15#1/r1.anchor: Form IV yunzil (anzala) vs standard Form II yunazzil (nazzala) — shifts from gradual/staged sending

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r1.claim: The question expresses astonishment at fearing powerless idols while not fearing association with the God who controls benefit, harm, and all affairs; the changed objects avoid equating God with idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r1.anchor: استفهام معناه التعجب والإنكار كأنه تعجب من فساد عقولهم حيث خوفوه خشبا وحجارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r2.claim: The conjunction links “you do not fear” to “how do I fear,” placing both under the same rebuke; the wording uses “what” because idols are non-rational objects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r2.anchor: ولا تخافون معطوف على أخاف فهو داخل في التعجب والإنكار واختلف متعلق الخوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r3.claim: “Authority” means proof: after rationally refuting the idols, Abraham also denies any revealed evidence for associating them with God, so shirk is invalid both rationally and scripturally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r3.anchor: والسلطان الحجة والإشراك لا يصح أن يكون عليه حجة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r4.claim: The reading “sulṭānan” with a ḍamma on lām is either a dialect that establishes this vocal pattern or vowel-following that does not establish it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r4.anchor: وقرئ سلطانا بضم اللام والخلاف هل ذلك لغة فيثبت به بناء فعلان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r5.claim: Abraham asks which of the two parties, idolaters or monotheists, deserves safety, presenting a known answer as an open question; he avoids saying “which of us” to avoid self-praise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r5.anchor: ويعني فريق المشركين وفريق الموحدين وعدل عن أينا أحق بالأمن أنا أم أنتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r6.claim: The conditional has an omitted answer: if they are knowledgeable and discerning, they should identify which party is safer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r6.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف أي إن كنتم من ذوي العلم والاستبصار فأخبروني

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r1.claim: The resumed question denies Abraham's fear according to the idolaters' own assumptions, after denying it in reality; asking how he could fear intensifies the total denial because every existent thing has some modality.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r1.anchor: استئناف كما قال شيخ الإسلام مسوق لنفي الخوف عنه عليه السلام بحسب زعم الكفرة بالطريق الإلزامي بعد نفيه عنه بحسب الواقع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r2.claim: 'How' is circumstantial; the object may be relative, indefinite with a modifier, or a verbal noun, with its antecedent omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r2.anchor: والاستفهام لإنكار الوقوع ونفيه بالكلية وفي توجيه الإنكار إلى كيفية الخوف من المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r3.claim: Their failure to fear their association of created things with God is a circumstantial clause reinforcing Abraham's denial and exposing their admission: if they do not fear in the place of fear, he is still less afraid in safety.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r3.anchor: وهو مقرر لإنكار الخوف ونفيه عنه عليه السلام ومفيد لاعترافهم بذلك فإنهم حيث لم يخافوا في محل الخوف

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r4.claim: The phrase 'an authority He did not send down' is a sarcastic name for their nonexistent proof and signals that religious claims must rest on proof revealed by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r4.anchor: أي حجة على طريق التهكم قيل مع الإيذان بأن الأمور الدينية لا يعول فيها إلا على الحجة المنزلة من عند الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r5.claim: The name 'God' appears in the second clause to magnify the offense of associating with Him; a proposed grammatical explanation that it supplies an antecedent for the next pronoun is rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205#2/r5.anchor: لأن المراد في الجملة الحالية تهويل الأمر وذكر المشرك به أدخل في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r1.speaker: some precise scholars
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r1.claim: One explanation for omitting God's name from the first clause is that the preceding verse already mentioned it, and Abraham avoids even suggesting association with God; its explicit mention in the second fits the idolaters' failure to sanctify Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r1.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : الظأهر أن يقال في وجه الذكر في الثانية والترك في الاولى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r2.claim: Al-Alusi rejects explaining the second mention merely as a needed pronoun antecedent or as a different scope of denial, since the antecedent was already available and the two clauses do not combine under one negation as claimed.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن ذكر الاسم الجليل في الجملة الثانية ليعود إليه الضمير في مالم ينرل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r3.claim: The verse explicitly says no divine warrant was revealed for shirk; the author chooses the position that such warrant is rationally impossible, while the Imam's analogy of idols as a prayer direction lies outside the dispute.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r3.anchor: والذي اختاره الأول وقول الامام إنه لا يمتنع عقلا أن يؤمر باتخاذ تلك التماثيل والصور

ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r4.claim: The question which group deserves security follows from the contrast between fear in a safe place and lack of fear in a dangerous one, compelling admission that Abraham merits safety and they do not.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r4.anchor: مسوق لالجائهم إلى الاعتراف باستحقاقه عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r5.claim: The comparative 'more entitled' gently assumes some possible entitlement to draw them from obstinacy; 'the two groups' avoids naming and blaming them directly and shows security belongs to every monotheist.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p206/r5.anchor: لاستنزالهم عن رتبة المكابرة والاعتساف بسوق الكلام على سنن الانصاف

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r1.claim: The question ends by asking which group is more deserving, or what they know; it may challenge them to answer if they are knowledgeable.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r1.anchor: أي من هو أحق بذلك أو شيء من الأشياء

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r2.claim: A reading pronounces the lām in 'sulṭān' with ḍamma, a dialectal vowel harmonization following the preceding ḍamma.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207/r2.anchor: بضم اللام وهي لغة اتبع فيها الضم الضم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r1.claim: What Abraham's opponents associate with God are idols that cannot see, hear, harm, or benefit; they should fear associating God with something for which no proof was sent, since God has power over all.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r1.anchor: {وكيف أخاف ما أشركتم} يعني الأصنام، وهي لا تبصر ولا تسمع ولا تضر ولا تنفع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r2.claim: Abraham asks which group is more entitled to safety: he and his religion's adherents, or the idolaters, if they understand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p164/r2.anchor: {فأي الفريقين أحق} أولى، {بالأمن} أنا وأهل ديني أم أنتم؟ {إن كنتم تعلمون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r1.claim: Abraham asks how he could fear powerless idols while his opponents do not fear associating created, powerless things with the creator, who alone can harm and benefit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r1.anchor: وهو حقيق بأن يخاف منه كل الخوف لأنه إشراك للمصنوع بالصانع، وتسوية بين المقدور العاجز بالقادر

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r2.claim: The idols have no revealed authority, meaning no scripture or proof supports their worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r2.anchor: ما لم ينزل بإشراكه كتابا، أو لم ينصب عليه دليلا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r3.claim: The factions are monotheists and polytheists; Abraham avoids asking which of us deserves safety to avoid self-praise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:81/r3.anchor: أي الموحدون أو المشركون، وإنما لم يقل أينا أنا أم أنتم احترازا من تزكية نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r7.claim: Abraham contrasts his lack of fear of powerless idols with their failure to fear God, who has power to punish them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r7.anchor: وتعجب منهم في ظنهم خوفه من معبوداتهم بقوله منكرا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r8.claim: Their idols have no revealed warrant that would shield them from God’s anger; mentioning and fronting “upon you” underscores the gravity of this foundational question.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r8.anchor: ولما كان المقام صعبا لأنه أصل الدين , أثبت الجار والمجرور وقدمه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r1.claim: Abraham explains that idols cannot harm, while this passage identifies fear of harm from them as the danger being denied.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r1.anchor: ولما كان المحذور المنفي هنا إنما هو خوف الضرر من آلهتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r2.claim: Abraham invokes God as Lord because the danger concerned harm and protection; Shuʿayb invokes the all-comprehensive divine name because the issue was returning to unbelief.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r2.anchor: اقتصر الخليل عليه السلام على صفة الربوبية المقتضية للرأفة والرحمة والكفاية والحماية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r3.claim: The two prophets’ conditional language comes from one source, as does the reminder not to claim certainty about tomorrow without God’s will.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r4.claim: “Which of the two parties” generalizes beyond Abraham and his people to God’s party and the idolaters’ party, compelling the audience to answer who deserves security.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p662/r4.anchor: أي إن كان لكم علم فأخبروني عما سألتكم عنه

DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.claim: Abraham’s people called him to worship another god and threatened him with their idols; he answered that he would not fear them, then challenged their failure to fear their unsupported association of partners with God.
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {وحاجه قومه} قال: دعوا مع الله إلها

DURR-FULL:v3p307/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r5.claim: Abraham asked his people which of the two parties had the better claim to security, making this one of his arguments.
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن} قال: قول إبراهيم حين سألهم

DURR-FULL:v3p307/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd contrasts fearing beings other than God without fearing God with fearing God without fearing others; God answers that security belongs to believers who do not mix faith with wrongdoing.
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r6.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن} أمن خاف غير الله ولم يخفه

MAJAZ:v1p200/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p200/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p200/r3.claim: Sulṭān means an authority, proof, argument, or excuse that God has not given them.
MAJAZ:v1p200/r3.anchor: «ما لم ينزل به [عليكم] سلطانا» (81) أي ما لم يجعل لكم فيه حجة، ولا برهانا، ولا عذرا.

BURHAN:v2p281/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p281/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p281/r1.claim: The heart can stand for intellect, mouths for tongues, tongue for language, and a village for its inhabitants.
BURHAN:v2p281/r1.anchor: والتعبير بالقلب عن الفعل كقوله ﴿ لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها ﴾ اي عقول

BURHAN:v2p281/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p281/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p281/r2.claim: A state may be named for its place: being in God's mercy means being in Paradise, plotting of night and day means plotting during them, and security or goodness predicated of a town describes its inhabitants or air.
BURHAN:v2p281/r2.anchor: إطلاق اسم الحال على المحل كقوله تعالى ﴿ وأما الذين ابيضت وجوههم ففي رحمة الله هم فيها خالدون ﴾

BURHAN:v2p281/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p281/r3.speaker: الحسن
BURHAN:v2p281/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reads “in your sleep” as “in your eye”; al-Zamakhshari regards that as remote and construes it as “in your vision.”
BURHAN:v2p281/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن في قوله ﴿ إذ يريكهم الله في منامك ﴾ اي في عينك واستبعده الزمخشري وقدر

BURHAN:v2p281/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p281/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p281/r4.claim: In “take your adornment at every mosque,” adornment means its place, while mosque means prayer; the former is an abstract state and the latter its place.
BURHAN:v2p281/r4.anchor: وقد اجتمع هذا والذي قبله في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا بني آدم خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد ﴾

BURHAN:v2p281/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p281/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p281/r5.claim: An instrument can name its effect: “a tongue of truth” means good remembrance, eyes mean God's sight, and a messenger's tongue means his people's language.
BURHAN:v2p281/r5.anchor: الثامن عشر إطلاق اسم آلة الشيء عليه كقوله تعالى ﴿ واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين ﴾

BURHAN:v2p281/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p281/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p281/r6.claim: A word can be transferred to its opposite: requital for an evil deed is called evil from the wrongdoer's perspective, though it is good from God; likewise obedience is called ihsan in a phrase about its reward.
BURHAN:v2p281/r6.anchor: التاسع عشر إطلاق اسم الضدين على الاخر كقوله تعالى ﴿ وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها ﴾

ITQAN:v2p426/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p426/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p426/r1.claim: The hamza is the basic interrogative particle: it asks for information and has features that distinguish it from other interrogatives.
ITQAN:v2p426/r1.anchor: أحدها الاستفهام وحقيقته طلب الإفهام وهي أصل أدواته ومن ثم اختصت بأمور

ITQAN:v2p426/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p426/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p426/r2.claim: Hamza can ask for either identification or confirmation, whereas hal asks only for confirmation and other interrogatives only for identification.
ITQAN:v2p426/r2.anchor: ثانيها أنها ترد لطلب التصور والتصديق بخلاف هل فإنها للتصديق خاصة وسائر الأدوات للتصور خاصة

ITQAN:v2p426/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p426/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p426/r3.claim: Hamza enters affirmative and negative clauses; with negation it can recall or alert, express astonishment at a grave matter, and warn.

ITQAN:v2p426/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p426/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p426/r4.claim: Hamza precedes conjunctions because it naturally takes the sentence's initial position; other interrogative particles follow the conjunction, as in this verse's فأي الفريقين.
ITQAN:v2p426/r4.anchor: رابعها تقديمها على العاطف تنبيها على إصالتها في التصدير

ITQAN:v2p426/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p426/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ITQAN:v2p426/r5.claim: An authority cited by Abu Hayyan says hamza is used when an assertion already weighs in the mind, unlike hal where neither affirmation nor denial predominates.

ITQAN:v2p426/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p426/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p426/r6.claim: Hamza can precede a conditional clause, a construction unavailable to the other interrogatives.

ITQAN:v2p426/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p426/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p426/r7.claim: Hamza can leave literal questioning for other rhetorical meanings, discussed in the fifty-seventh Qur'anic-sciences section.
ITQAN:v2p426/r7.anchor: وتخرج عن الاستفهام الحقيقي فتأتي لمعان تذكر في النوع السابع والخمسين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r1.claim: Sulṭān is formed on the pattern فعْلان from salāṭa, meaning forceful extension or dominance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r1.anchor: السلطان : فعلان من السلاطة وهي الانبساط بالقوة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r2.claim: One Qur'anic sense of sulṭān is kingship or coercive power, as in Satan's denial that he had power over people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r2.anchor: أحدهما : الملك والقهر . ومنه قوله تعالى في إبراهيم : ﴿ وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r3.claim: The other Qur'anic sense is proof or authority; the entry gives examples in 6:81, 11:96, 17:33, 30:35, 27:21, and 55:33.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p344/r3.anchor: والثاني : الحجة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام : ﴿ ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا ﴾

BURHAN:v3p399/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p399/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p399/r4.claim: The phrase ‘for which He sent down no authority’ denies both the reality of the alleged partners and the existence of any revealed proof for associating them.
BURHAN:v3p399/r4.anchor: أي شركاء لا ثبوت لها أصلا ولا أنزل الله بإشراكها حجة

BURHAN:v2p344/r1.claim: One rhetorical question can combine denial and affirmation: “Which group is more entitled to security?” denies security to the unbelievers and affirms it for believers.
BURHAN:v2p344/r1.anchor: أي ليس الكفار أمنين والذين آمنوا أحق بالآمن ولما كان أكثر مواقع التقرير دون الإنكار
